does: Cooks food close to fierce, direct heat, so that its surface colours and chars lightly while the inside stays moist.

intro.what: Grilling uses fierce direct heat close to the food to brown and lightly char its surface.
intro.why: It teaches you to judge surface colour and adjust distance from heat for thicker pieces.

how: Heat the grill until it is very hot before the food goes near it.
Dry the food, oil it lightly and season it.
Set it close to the heat and leave it until the surface has coloured, then turn it once.
Move a thick piece further from the heat once it has coloured, so that the inside can catch up.
For cheese on toast, set it a little further from the heat and take it out when the cheese has softened and browned on top.

cues.text: An evenly browned or blistered surface, with no black, bitter patches.
A smell of toasting, not of burning.

mistakes.mistake: Grilling food straight from the fridge, so that the outside burns before the inside is warm.
mistakes.fix: Let it lose its chill first.

mistakes.mistake: Turning it again and again, so that it never colours.
mistakes.fix: Leave it alone until it has coloured, then turn it once.

quiz.question: What does the direct heat of grilling develop?
choices: A pale surface softened in liquid.
A thick wet coating without colour.
quiz.because: Fierce direct heat colours the surface, with light charring rather than bitter black patches.

quiz.question: How should you turn food in this grilling method?
choices: Leave it until the surface colours, then turn.
Turn constantly from the moment it meets the heat.
Turn before any colour can form.
quiz.because: Leaving the surface still long enough lets it colour before turning.

quiz.question: Which smell matches the intended result?
choices: A raw scent with little toasted aroma.
quiz.because: A toasted scent accompanies browning; a burnt smell suggests the surface has gone too far.

quiz.question: A thick piece has coloured outside before the inside warms. What would you change?
choices: Move it closer to colour the outside faster.
Keep it close and turn it more rapidly.
Move it farther from the heat.
quiz.because: Greater distance after colouring gives the inside time to warm without burning the surface.
